bull.b: The absence of debt and substantial liquidity provide financial flexibility while Streamex develops its platform. Management estimates immediately available funds cover about 18 months at the expected burn rate, reducing near-term financing pressure and allowing time to pursue commercialization.

Completed custody, attestation, brokerage and liquidity capabilities strengthen the platform’s readiness for institutional participation. These integrations can reduce onboarding friction, improve product credibility, and support distribution as prospective institutional holders complete diligence.

The sharp sequential reduction in operating expenses indicates management has begun tightening the cost structure rather than relying solely on future growth. If maintained, lower operating costs can extend liquidity runway and reduce the revenue scale required to approach break-even.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated revenue scale capable of absorbing its cost base. Extremely large losses relative to revenue weaken earnings quality and make sustainable profitability dependent on substantial adoption, improved economics, or further cost reductions.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not currently self-funding and remains dependent on its liquidity and outside funding sources. Continued burn could reduce strategic flexibility before tokenized-gold revenue reaches a meaningful recurring scale.

Unresolved control weaknesses can undermine reporting reliability and increase compliance and execution burdens as the company expands institutional operations. Until remediation is completed and demonstrated, the issue remains a structural governance risk for scaling the business.
